decisions.item_text: In the risk assessment of each excipient, based on its source, supply chain and intended use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers at minimum whether everyone working in manufacturing and quality activities is covered by a training programme.
decisions.reason: Training for all manufacturing and quality staff is not covered by the listed excipient requirements; the existing training item covers only health, hygiene and clothing.

decisions.item_text: The quality system is designed, planned, put in place, maintained and continually improved so that products with suitable quality attributes are delivered consistently.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers designing and improving the quality system for consistent product quality.

decisions.item_text: Knowledge of the product and the process is managed at every stage of the lifecycle.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers lifecycle knowledge management.

decisions.item_text: Medicinal products are designed and developed with GMP requirements taken into account.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers taking GMP into account in product design and development.

decisions.item_text: Production and control operations are clearly defined and carried out under GMP.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers clearly defined production and control operations under GMP.

decisions.item_text: Management responsibilities are clearly defined.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers clearly defined management responsibilities.

decisions.item_text: Arrangements are in place for making, supplying and using the correct starting and packaging materials, for choosing and monitoring suppliers, and for checking that every delivery comes from the approved supply chain.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers material supply arrangements and supplier selection and monitoring for the finished-product manufacturer.

decisions.item_text: Processes are in place for managing outsourced activities.
decisions.reason: The listed outsourcing requirement covers only approval of contract manufacturers, not general management of outsourced activities.

decisions.item_text: Process performance and product quality are monitored and controlled through effective systems that bring about and keep a state of control.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers a state of control through monitoring systems.

decisions.item_text: Results from monitoring products and processes are used in batch release, in deviation investigations and for preventive action to avoid future deviations.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers use of monitoring results in release, investigations and prevention.

decisions.item_text: Every necessary check on intermediate products, together with other in-process controls and validations, is performed.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers performing intermediate and in-process controls and validations.

decisions.item_text: Quality improvements suited to the current level of process and product knowledge are put in place to support continual improvement.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers continual improvement through quality improvements.

decisions.item_text: Planned changes are evaluated in advance and approved before they are implemented, with regulatory notification and approval taken into account where required.
decisions.reason: The listed change requirement is about quality unit approval only; prospective evaluation with regulatory consideration is a separate point.

decisions.item_text: After a change is implemented, it is evaluated to confirm that its quality objectives were met and that product quality was not unintentionally harmed.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers post-implementation evaluation of changes.

decisions.item_text: Investigations of deviations, suspected product defects and other problems use a suitable depth of root cause analysis.
decisions.reason: The listed deviation requirement covers investigation and resolution, not the depth of root cause analysis.

decisions.item_text: When the true root cause of a problem cannot be determined, the most likely root cause or causes are identified and addressed.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers handling an undeterminable root cause.

decisions.item_text: A conclusion that human error caused a problem, whether suspected or confirmed, is justified only after confirming that no process, procedural or system-based errors or problems were missed.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers justifying human error as a root cause.

decisions.item_text: Suitable corrective and/or preventive actions are identified and taken in response to investigations.
decisions.reason: The listed corrective action requirement is limited to self-inspection; CAPA after investigations is not listed.

decisions.item_text: The effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions is monitored and assessed in line with quality risk management principles.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers monitoring CAPA effectiveness.

decisions.item_text: No medicinal product is sold or supplied until the certifying person (Qualified Person or Authorised Person) has certified that each production batch was made and controlled in line with the marketing authorisation and any other rules on production, control and release.
decisions.reason: The listed release requirements concern the quality unit for active substances, not certification of medicinal product batches before supply.

decisions.item_text: Arrangements are in place to make sure, as far as possible, that medicinal products are stored, distributed and handled afterwards in a way that keeps their quality throughout their shelf life.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers arrangements to keep quality during storage, distribution and handling.

decisions.item_text: A self-inspection and/or quality audit process regularly appraises how effective and applicable the quality system is.
decisions.reason: The listed self-inspection requirements check GMP compliance; appraising the quality system's effectiveness is a separate point.

decisions.item_text: The manufacturer, and the marketing authorisation holder where different, evaluate the results of the product quality review and assess within the quality system whether corrective and preventive action or revalidation is needed.
decisions.reason: The listed review requirement covers performing the review, not evaluating its results for CAPA or revalidation.

decisions.item_text: Management procedures are in place for the ongoing management and review of actions arising from the product quality review.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers procedures for managing actions from product quality reviews.

decisions.item_text: Self-inspection verifies the effectiveness of the procedures for managing and reviewing actions arising from the product quality review.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers verifying those procedures during self-inspection.

decisions.item_text: Where scientifically justified, product quality reviews may be grouped by product type, for example solid, liquid or sterile dosage forms.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers grouping of product quality reviews.

decisions.item_text: Where the marketing authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, a technical agreement sets out each party's responsibilities for producing the product quality review.
decisions.reason: No listed requirement covers a technical agreement on review responsibilities.
